defects.description: main_test.go has no build tag, and the new test calls os.Symlink without a skip. On native Windows without symlink privilege or Developer Mode it fails with t.Fatal instead of t.Skip. This is latent: Windows tests are not run today, but a native X1 run would hit it.

The comment says a link retargeted after the pre-check is refused. The block only calls openNoBlock and f.Stat directly on a FIFO link. No test injects a swap between Stat and open through Load, so the fstat and os.SameFile path stays unexercised and the comment overstates the coverage.

The test depends on timing. It waits a fixed 600 ms before sending 'q' and 100 ms to drain output before checking the alt-screen leave sequence. Existing pty tests use the same pattern, and the test passed 5 of 5 reviewer reruns on darwin, but it could flake on a loaded host.

Symlinks are now followed on Windows too, where they used to be refused. The comment there still says Stat has already refused non-regular paths, so a plain open cannot block. For a followed link that can be retargeted after the check, the comment was not revisited. The descriptor check still refuses non-regular files, and this path is compile-checked only.

reviewer_probes.observed: no output (test code compiles for windows-amd64; not run)
